clinicalNotes.title: Emergency H&P: Acute Popliteal DVT
clinicalNotes.text:
Rajesh Sharma is a 54-year-old male presenting with painful swelling of the right calf and popliteal fossa following a 14-hour international flight.
Venous Doppler ultrasound confirms extensive occlusive thrombus in the right popliteal and posterior tibial veins.
Baseline labs: INR 1.0, Platelets 240k.
Started on Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg BID bridge and Warfarin 5 mg daily.

clinicalNotes.title: Inpatient Medicine Progress Note
clinicalNotes.text: Patient ambulatory with compression stockings. Warfarin dose maintained at 5 mg daily. INR today is 1.4. Continuing Lovenox bridging.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-201 DVT Initiation
clinicalNotes.text: Patient discharged with INR 2.1. Lovenox discontinued. Instructions provided for weekly INR monitoring at Anticoagulation Clinic. Maintain Warfarin 5 mg daily.

clinicalNotes.title: Anticoagulation Clinic Note: Subtherapeutic INR
clinicalNotes.text:
INR check today reveals subtherapeutic result: 1.4. Patient reports missing two doses last week due to work travel and increased dietary vitamin K (green salads).
Warfarin dose adjusted to 7.5 mg on Mondays/Thursdays, 5 mg other days. Recheck INR in 10 days.

clinicalNotes.title: H&P: Bilateral Pulmonary Embolism & Warfarin Failure
clinicalNotes.text:
CLINICAL EVALUATION:
Patient presents with sudden-onset sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath.
CT Pulmonary Angiogram shows bilateral subsegmental pulmonary emboli.
CONTRADICTION IN RECORD:
Attending Physician Dr. House writes: "Patient has suffered recurrent venous thromboembolism while supposedly on anticoagulation. Laboratory testing shows INR is critically subtherapeutic at 1.5, demonstrating failure and unreliability of Warfarin therapy."
(NOTE: Electronic Laboratory result LAB-205 from the exact same morning shows INR 2.8!).
PLAN:
Permanently discontinue Warfarin. Switch to Direct Oral Anticoagulant: Apixaban (Eliquis) 10 mg BID x 7 days followed by 5 mg BID maintenance. Metformin held temporarily due to iodinated CT contrast exposure.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Severe contradiction: Physician writes INR is 1.5, but official lab LAB-205 reports INR 2.8.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-202 Switch to Apixaban
clinicalNotes.text:
Patient chest pain fully resolved. Oxygen saturation 98% room air.
Discharged on Apixaban 5 mg BID (following 7-day loading phase).
Warfarin discontinued. Metformin resumed at 1000 mg BID as creatinine normalized to 1.1 mg/dL.

clinicalNotes.title: Outpatient Follow-Up: Apixaban Tolerance
clinicalNotes.text: Patient reports excellent compliance with Apixaban 5 mg BID. No recurrent leg swelling or dyspnea. No bruising or bleeding noted. HbA1c 7.8%.

clinicalNotes.title: H&P: Lower GI Bleed on Apixaban
clinicalNotes.text:
Patient woke with lightheadedness and passed two large maroon stools with clots (hematochezia).
Admission Hemoglobin: 8.4 g/dL (down from baseline 14.2 g/dL).
Apixaban immediately held. Transfused 1 unit packed red blood cells. Urgent gastroenterology consult requested.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-203 Bleed Resolution
clinicalNotes.text:
Colonoscopy revealed diverticular hemorrhage in sigmoid colon, successfully treated with endoscopic hemoclips. Hemoglobin stable at 10.1 g/dL without further transfusion.
Given unprovoked PE history 8 months ago, anticoagulation cannot be completely stopped. Multi-disciplinary team consensus decided to resume Apixaban at a reduced dose of 2.5 mg BID with close monitoring.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Explains dose reduction of Apixaban from 5mg BID to 2.5mg BID.
